title: SQUEA: Soft-Quota + Advisory Eviction for Prefix-Safe KV Cache (correctness guarantees + rollout plan)
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We need an eviction mechanism for the GPU KV cache that balances latency SLOs, throughput (batching efficiency), and strong correctness guarantees for prefix-coherent workloads. Existing LRU/TTL/hybrid designs either violate prefix atomicity under concurrent access patterns or force too-aggressive trimming that regresses latency due to cold KV misses.

Proposal (SQUEA - Soft-Quota + Advisory Eviction):
1) Soft quotas per prefix group: each prefix (or logical prefix cohort) is given a soft memory quota instead of a hard cap. Quotas are sized from historical token-prefix distributions and can be exceeded temporarily with an associated "staleness credit" tracked per prefix.
2) Advisory eviction phase: when global memory pressure approaches a threshold, eviction is performed in two phases: (a) advisory marking (cheap): candidate entries are marked with an eviction score that accounts for last-access, ttl, prefix-credit, and contribution to batching (hot-spot affinity); (b) commit phase (safe): eviction commits only if doing so will not violate a prefix-safe contract for any in-flight batch or pinned KV window.
3) In-flight safety contract: before evicting keys that could be referenced by active GPU kernels (batch windows), the scheduler verifies an explicit handshake with the inference execution planner. If a key is potentially live (within the suffix window of a running batch), eviction is deferred or coordinated with a copy-on-evict flow to remote memory.
4) Staleness credit reclamation: prefixes that exceed quota accrue credit debt; we reclaim debt via prioritized TTL shortening and selective pinning trade-offs (evict low-value entries first). Credits decay back toward zero under reduced pressure, enabling bursty workloads without permanent loss of capacity to other prefixes.

Correctness guarantees we aim to provide:
- Prefix-consistency: No eviction may render the KV state observed by any completed inference request inconsistent with what would be produced if the cache were infinite (modulo expected TTL semantics).
- Atomicity for batched requests: For any batched inference that reads multiple KV entries for a prefix, either all required KV entries are retained for the duration of the batch or the scheduler performs transparent fallback (remote fetch or short stall) to preserve deterministic outputs.
- Bounded staleness: When eviction occurs, the maximum additional staleness introduced (compared to ideal infinite cache) is bounded and parameterized by the configured soft-quota and credit windows.

Design trade-offs and mitigations:
- Latency vs memory pressure: advisory marking adds a small compute overhead but avoids costly mistaken evictions that introduce tail latency. We will measure overhead on p4d and a100 testbeds and gate rollout by 99th-percentile stall impact (< 2ms overhead target).
- Complexity vs observability: SQUEA introduces several new counters (credits, eviction-scores, advisory-flags). We will add trace events and a dedicated console panel under "KV Eviction Insights" showing prefix-credit burn, advisory commit rates, and last-seen batch handshake latencies.
- Failure modes: to avoid deadlocks between eviction and inference kernels we specify a non-blocking fallback: if the handshake times out, the scheduler will fall back to a pre-configured policy (pin or remote-copy) and record an incident metric for postmortem.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (spec + simulation): formalize the prefix-safety contract and build a simulator that replays production trace to validate bounded-staleness properties. Deliverable: correctness proof sketch + simulation report.
- Phase 2 (runtime prototype): implement advisory marking and soft-quotas in the cache manager with an opt-in runtime flag. Add RPC handshake hooks to the inference planner. Deliverable: feature behind flag + perf test harness.
- Phase 3 (canary rollout): small percentage of traffic on dedicated clusters with metrics wired to Console. Observe 99/95/50 p99 token latency and KV miss rates.
- Phase 4 (gradual ramp + hardened tests): add fuzz tests, eviction-atomicity integration tests, and a migration plan for existing pinned keys.

Metrics and success criteria:
- No regression in 99th-percentile generation latency under representative workloads (target < 5% regression).
- KV-induced stalls for in-flight batches limited to < 0.1% of requests at canary.
- Reduction in unnecessary eviction re-fetches (measured as re-fetch ratio) by at least 25% vs current TTL-only baseline.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Console dashboards: new "KV Eviction Insights" chart, prefix-credit heatmap, advisory->commit ratio.
- Alerts: spike in handshake timeouts, commit-phase eviction rate increasing > 10x baseline, or re-fetch ratio > 2x baseline.
- Safety switches: runtime flag to disable advisory commit path and revert to LRU-ttl fallback.

Open questions (to resolve in Phase 1):
- How to pick prefix cohort granularity for multi-tenant customers (per-customer vs per-application vs learned clusters).
- Optimal decay schedule for staleness credits to balance fairness and burst tolerance.
- Interaction with quantized model variants where KV entry sizes and value importance differ significantly.

2025-02-18 - Maya Chen: Feasibility follow-up from implementation perspective: advisory marking fits into the existing cache manager; need API from planner to query in-flight windows. Filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1421

2025-02-21 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Noted that handshake timeouts could correlate with our RPC tail latencies; proposed using bounded async handshake with optimistic eviction path. Added to open questions.
2025-02-25 - Design review (Sofia Morales): Suggested console wireframes for prefix-credit heatmap. Linked mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/kv-eviction-heatmap-v1

2025-02-28 - Arjun Patel: Completed initial simulator run on a 7-day production trace. Results: average advisory->commit ratio 3.5:1, re-fetch ratio down 32% versus TTL baseline. Uploaded report: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/SQUEA-simulation-2025-02

2025-03-03 - Maya Chen: Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1987. Prototype implements soft-quotas and advisory marking behind feature flag. Seeking design + perf review.

2025-03-04 - Perf team (Nikhil Rao): Ran microbench on p4d: advisory marking adds 0.6ms median, 1.9ms p99 overhead for the cache manager path under worst-case churn. This is within the 2ms gate; will continue to profile commit-phase costs.
